sections.title: 8. Where State Machine DP Shows Up

blocks.text: Before patterns and code, let's understand what a state machine is and how DP fits into it.
A state machine is a system that is always in one of a fixed set of states. Based on what happens, it moves from one state to another.
At any moment, it is in exactly one state.
An event (or timer) causes it to transition to the next state.
In programming problems, the "states" are not traffic lights they are conditions your solution can be in at any point during processing.
<hr style="border-width: 1px medium medium; border-style: solid none none; border-color: rgb(224, 224, 224) currentcolor currentcolor; border-image: none; margin: 24px 0px;">
State Machine DP is when:

items: Your problem has a fixed set of conditions (states).
You transition between states based on the decisions you make.
Each transition has an associated cost or gain.
Your goal is to optimize the total cost or gain.

blocks.text: Instead of onedp[i]value per position, you maintain one value per state per position:
/engineering/dsa-media/1785406280357-740960775.png
The Classic Example Stock Buy and Sell
You have stock prices over n days. You can buy and sell. Find maximum profit.
/engineering/dsa-media/1785406280357-169908046.png
blocks.alt: The Classic Example Stock Buy and Sell

blocks.text: At any day, you are in exactly one of two states:

items: State 0 → you do not hold a stock (you can buy)
State 1 → you do hold a stock (you can sell)

blocks.text: That's your state machine:
/engineering/dsa-media/1785406280358-432882901.png
blocks.alt: The Classic Example Stock Buy and Sell

items: From State 0 (no stock)→ you can buy→ move to State 1
From State 1 (holding)→ you can sell→ move to State 0
From either state→ you can do nothing→ stay in the same state

blocks.text: <hr style="border-width: 1px medium medium; border-style: solid none none; border-color: rgb(224, 224, 224) currentcolor currentcolor; border-image: none; margin: 24px 0px;">
At each day you make a decision. That decision determines which state you move to:
/engineering/dsa-media/1785406280358-582931735.png
State Transitions with Actions:
If you are in State 0 (no stock):

items: Do nothing → stay in State 0
Buy → move to State 1, pay prices[i]

blocks.text: If you are in State 1 (holding stock):

items: Do nothing → stay in State 1
Sell → move to State 0, gain prices[i]

blocks.text: Translated into recurrence:
/engineering/dsa-media/1785406280358-314592799.png
DP Transitions:

codes.javascript:
dp[i][0] = max(
  dp[i−1][0],                   // do nothing, stay in state 0
  dp[i−1][1] + prices[i]       // sell today, move from state 1
)

dp[i][1] = max(
  dp[i−1][1],                  // do nothing, stay in state 1
  dp[i−1][0] − prices[i].      // buy today, move from state 0
)

blocks.text: Meaning:

items: dp[i][0] → max profit on day i when you do not hold stock
dp[i][1] → max profit on day i when you do hold stock

blocks.text: The most important step in state machine DP draw the states and transitions before writing any code.
/engineering/dsa-media/1785406280358-158787003.png
Three states now:
/engineering/dsa-media/1785406280772-734279724.png
States (with cooldown):

items:
State 0 → ready to buy
(not holding a stock, not in cooldown)

State 1 → holding a stock
(already bought, waiting to sell)

State 2 → in cooldown
(just sold, must wait one day before buying again)

blocks.text: Transitions:
State Transitions (with cooldown):

items: State 0 → State 0: do nothing
State 0 → State 1: buy stock, pay prices[i]
State 1 → State 1: do nothing
State 1 → State 2: sell stock, gain prices[i]
State 2 → State 0: cooldown ends, become ready to buy again

blocks.text: Recurrence:
Meaning:

items: dp[i][0] → ready to buy (no stock, no cooldown)
dp[i][1] → currently holding a stock
dp[i][2] → in cooldown (just sold)

blocks.text: <hr style="border-width: 1px medium medium; border-style: solid none none; border-color: rgb(224, 224, 224) currentcolor currentcolor; border-image: none; margin: 24px 0px;">
Adding Transaction Limits
If you can make at most K transactions, you add another dimension to your state to track how many transactions have been used.
DP State:

codes.javascript: dp[i][k][state] = maximum profit on day i with k transactions used and current state

items: state 0 → not holding a stock
state 1 → holding a stock

blocks.text: Recurrence:

codes.javascript:
dp[i][k][0] = max(
  dp[i−1][k][0],        // rest
  dp[i−1][k][1] + prices[i] // sell (completes a transaction)
)

dp[i][k][1] = max(
  dp[i−1][k][1],         // rest
  dp[i−1][k−1][0] − prices[i] // buy (starts a new transaction)
)

blocks.text: A transaction is counted when youbuy, so buying reduces your remaining transactions by 1.
Every state-machine DP problem follows the same structure:

Step 1: Identify all possible states
What conditions can you be in at any point?

Step 2: Define transitions between states
What decisions move you from one state to another?
What is the cost or gain of each transition?

Step 3: Define dp[i][state]
Best result at position i while in this state

Step 4: Write base cases
What is the value of each state at position 0?

Step 5: Fill the table
For each position, update each state using transitions from the previous position

Step 6: Read the answer
Usually max or min over all states at the last position
The key idea behind state-machine DP is that future decisions depend not just on position, but also on the current state.
Without state tracking:

codes.javascript: dp[i] = best profit up to day i

blocks.text: Problem
With state tracking:

items: dp[i][0] = best profit up to day i, not holding
dp[i][1] = best profit up to day i, holding

blocks.text: Now you retain complete information needed for optimal decisions.
Space Optimization
You usually only need values from the previous step:

items: Full DP → O(n × states)
Optimized → O(states) using two arrays: previous and current

blocks.text: Swap them at each step instead of storing the entire table.

Core takeaway:

State = memory of the system. Without it, DP loses context. With it, decisions become optimal
Space reduces fromO(n × states)toO(states).

content.title: 8. Where State Machine DP Shows Up

items: Stock trading problems → holding / not holding / cooldown
Text parsing → inside word / outside word / escape character
Game states → attacking / defending / stunned
Pattern matching → matched k characters / failed / succeeded
Robot movement → direction / fuel remaining / visited

blocks.text: Anytime you have a process that moves through well-defined phases based on decisions, it forms a state machine and DP can be used to optimize it.
